nodes.title: Dirichlet weighted-string adjacent-gap box problem
nodes.statement: For R>1, K_R is the set of a.e. equivalence classes rho in L-infinity(0,1) with 1<=rho<=R a.e.; lambda_k(rho) are the increasingly ordered Dirichlet eigenvalues of -y''=lambda rho y on (0,1), and D_n(rho)=lambda_{n+1}(rho)-lambda_n(rho).

nodes.title: Bang-bang density and effective switch count
nodes.statement: A density rho in K_R is bang-bang with at most m switches when, after merging adjacent equal-value cells, it equals 1 or R a.e. on the cells of a partition 0=x_0<x_1<...<x_j<x_{j+1}=1 with j<=m.

nodes.title: All-n adjacent-gap parameter domain
nodes.statement: R is a real number with R>1 and n is an integer with n>=2.

nodes.title: Existence of adjacent-gap extrema
nodes.statement: For every R>1 and integer n>=2, D_n attains its maximum and minimum on K_R.

nodes.title: At most 2n switching-function zeros
nodes.statement: For every rho in K_R, if u_n and u_{n+1} are weighted-L2 normalized consecutive Dirichlet eigenfunctions, then F_n=lambda_n u_n^2-lambda_{n+1}u_{n+1}^2 has at most 2n distinct zeros in (0,1) and no positive-measure zero set.

nodes.title: Every adjacent-gap extremizer is bang-bang
nodes.statement: For every R>1 and integer n>=2, every global maximizer and minimizer of D_n on K_R takes only the values 1 and R almost everywhere, and every effective switch lies in the zero set of its F_n.

nodes.title: All-n finite-block reduction for adjacent gaps
nodes.statement: For every R>1 and integer n>=2, D_n attains both extrema on K_R, and every global maximizer and minimizer is bang-bang a.e. with at most 2n switches and hence at most 2n+1 constant blocks.

nodes.title: Weak-star compactness and spectral convergence imply existence
nodes.statement: Weak-star compactness of K_R and continuity of the relevant eigenvalues imply CLM-NGE2-EXISTENCE.

nodes.title: Wronskian quotient monotonicity implies the 2n zero bound
nodes.statement: Sturm interlacing and a strict-sign Wronskian show that u_{n+1}/u_n is strictly monotone on each nodal interval of u_n, which implies CLM-NGE2-ZERO-BOUND.

nodes.title: Box-constrained first variation implies bang-bang saturation
nodes.statement: The Feynman-Hellmann first variation, box-constraint needle variations, and CLM-NGE2-ZERO-BOUND imply CLM-NGE2-BANGBANG.

nodes.title: Existence, zero count, and saturation imply finite reduction
nodes.statement: CLM-NGE2-EXISTENCE, CLM-NGE2-ZERO-BOUND, and CLM-NGE2-BANGBANG imply CLM-NGE2-FINITE-REDUCTION.

nodes.title: Prove or refute the all-n finite-block reduction
nodes.statement: Determine whether CLM-NGE2-FINITE-REDUCTION is true in CTX-DEFAULT.
nodes.quantifier_contract: For every real R>1, every integer n>=2, and every global maximizer or minimizer rho_* in K_R, existence, bang-bang saturation, and the at-most-2n switch bound must hold.
boundary_cases: Measurable weights and weak-star oscillatory sequences.
The first and last nodal intervals and common Dirichlet endpoint zeros.
R approaches 1 from above, arbitrary finite R, inactive switches, and positive-measure switching-function zero sets.

nodes.title: Weak-star spectral continuity
nodes.statement: Prove the compactness and spectral-continuity step required by INF-NGE2-EXISTENCE.
nodes.formal_statement: If rho_j converges weak-star to rho in K_R, then lambda_k(rho_j) converges to lambda_k(rho) for every fixed k, and consequently D_n attains both extrema on K_R.
discharge_criteria: Give both limsup and liminf arguments without adding regularity to rho.
Handle eigenfunction subsequences and normalization explicitly.

nodes.title: Strict quotient monotonicity on all nodal intervals
nodes.statement: Prove the strict Wronskian sign and quotient monotonicity needed by INF-NGE2-ZERO-BOUND.
nodes.formal_statement: After orienting consecutive eigenfunctions consistently, W=u_{n+1}'u_n-u_{n+1}u_n' has one strict sign on (0,1), so u_{n+1}/u_n is strictly monotone on each component of {u_n!=0}.
discharge_criteria: Use interlacing to control every nodal-cell endpoint sign.
Include one-sided limits at 0, 1, and poles.

nodes.title: First variation and pointwise saturation
nodes.statement: Prove the Feynman-Hellmann and needle-variation steps required by INF-NGE2-BANGBANG.
nodes.formal_statement: At a box-constrained global extremizer, all admissible L-infinity directions give the correct one-sided derivative of D_n, forcing rho to saturate to 1 or R wherever F_n is nonzero.

nodes.statement: Attack the all-n zero bound by a strict-sign Wronskian and two level crossings per nodal interval.

nodes.title: Canonical orientation and endpoint norming ratios
nodes.statement: For R>1, integer n>=2, and rho in K_R, let u_k (k=n,n+1) be the unique real eigenfunction satisfying integral_0^1 rho u_k^2=1 and u_k'(0)>0. Define c=sqrt(lambda_n/lambda_{n+1})>0, q_0=u_{n+1}'(0)/u_n'(0)>0, and q_1=u_{n+1}'(1)/u_n'(1). Dirichlet simplicity makes all displayed endpoint derivatives nonzero, so these quantities are unambiguous; the sign of q_1 is a proof consequence, not part of the convention.

nodes.title: Endpoint norming constants determine the exact zero and switch count
nodes.statement: For every R>1, every integer n>=2, and every rho in K_R, use DEF-NGE2-ENDPOINT-NORMING and put F_n=lambda_n u_n^2-lambda_{n+1}u_{n+1}^2. Then F_n has exactly 2n-2+1_{q_0>c}+1_{q_1<-c} distinct interior zeros. If rho is a global extremizer, every one of these simple zeros is an effective switch, so rho has exactly 2n switches if and only if q_0>c and q_1<-c.

nodes.title: Maximizer endpoint norming rigidity
nodes.statement: For every R>1 and integer n>=2, every global maximizer rho_* of D_n on K_R satisfies q_0>c and q_1<-c with the uniquely oriented weighted-L2 normalized eigenfunctions and notation fixed by DEF-NGE2-ENDPOINT-NORMING.

nodes.title: Minimizer endpoint norming rigidity
nodes.statement: For every R>1 and integer n>=2, every global minimizer rho_* of D_n on K_R satisfies q_0>c and q_1<-c with the uniquely oriented weighted-L2 normalized eigenfunctions and notation fixed by DEF-NGE2-ENDPOINT-NORMING.

nodes.title: Every adjacent-gap maximizer has exactly 2n switches

nodes.title: Every adjacent-gap minimizer has exactly 2n switches
nodes.statement: For every R>1 and integer n>=2, every global minimizer of D_n on K_R has exactly 2n effective switches after adjacent equal-value blocks are merged.

nodes.statement: For every R>1, every integer n>=2, and every global maximizer or global minimizer rho_* of D_n on K_R, rho_* has exactly 2n effective switches after adjacent equal-value blocks are merged.

nodes.statement: For an arbitrary global adjacent-gap extremizer, the accepted finite bang-bang reduction and switch-zero condition imply a global block-energy difference K=-2(lambda_{n+1}-lambda_n), and hence strict endpoint derivative-magnitude inequalities.

nodes.title: Global energy invariant and strict endpoint slope dominance
nodes.statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, and every global maximizer or minimizer rho_* of D_n on K_R, use DEF-NGE2-ENDPOINT-NORMING and any finite bang-bang representative. The blockwise quantity K=(u_n'^2+lambda_n rho_* u_n^2)-(u_{n+1}'^2+lambda_{n+1} rho_* u_{n+1}^2) glues across every effective switch to the global a.e. constant -2D_n(rho_*). Consequently q_0>1 and q_1<-1.

nodes.title: Multi-phase O3a self-consistency
nodes.statement: For R>1, integer n>=2, and rho in K_R, normalize the consecutive Dirichlet eigenfunctions by integral rho u_k^2=1 and define F_{n,rho}=lambda_n u_n^2-lambda_{n+1}u_{n+1}^2. A max-self-consistent 2n-phase point is a bang-bang rho with exactly 2n effective switches and rho=R a.e. on {F_{n,rho}>0}, rho=1 a.e. on {F_{n,rho}<0}; a min-self-consistent point obeys the reversed law. Values on the zero set are identified a.e.; effective switches are positive-length cell boundaries and must be zeros of F_{n,rho}.

nodes.title: Max multi-phase O3a uniqueness
nodes.statement: For every finite R>1 and integer n>=2, any two max-self-consistent 2n-phase points in the sense of DEF-NGE2-MPO3A-SELFCONSISTENCY coincide a.e.; consequently the unique point, when it exists, is reflection invariant.

nodes.title: Structural closure of multiphase self-consistent points
nodes.statement: For every finite R>1 and n>=2, any bang-bang weight with exactly 2n effective switches all lying in the switching-function zero set has global difference energy K=-2(lambda_{n+1}-lambda_n), endpoint ratios q_L>1 and q_R<-1, and exactly those 2n switches as all interior zeros of F, each simple and ordered by quotient crossings +c,-c,... . Hence every max/min self-consistent point has forced endpoint materials 1/R respectively, forced nodal-cell allocation, no tangencies, inactive zeros, zero intervals or hidden extra zeros, and reflection preserves its sign class.

nodes.title: Interface-energy balance gives the exact multiphase phase defect

nodes.title: Exact internal phase-defect law and obstruction to the old O3a proof
nodes.statement: For every finite R>1, n>=2, sign and self-consistent point, with endpoint phases alpha,beta, tau=sqrt(lambda_{n+1}/lambda_n), sigma equal to the inner/outer material ratio, and S the alternating internal interface-amplitude sum defined in the proof package, S=2(lambda_{n+1}-lambda_n)[h_{tau,sigma}(beta)-h_{tau,sigma}(alpha)]. For max, h is strictly decreasing and alpha=beta iff S=0. For min, unrestricted global monotonicity of the same h is false: tau=4/3, sigma=1/100, t=3pi/5 gives h'(t)>0 exactly. The n=1 proof has empty S, whereas n>=2 has no self-consistency equation forcing S=0.

Do not infer partial_mu A_n>0 from partial_q A_n>0 or fixed-mu cell order without a noncircular fixed-q frequency or equivalent global response estimate.
Any counterexample must satisfy the full physical relay, common-terminal, event-count, and transversality predicates; scalar ledgers and local-cell witnesses do not discharge this obligation.

nodes.title: Max common-terminal A_mu Wronskian and compactified boundary route
nodes.statement: Use exact parameter Wronskians, Pohozaev identities, a uniform R=1 labelled word, and a blown-up q-to-infinity event-pair analysis to orient partial_mu A_n at both boundary regimes. The finite-contrast bounded-q interior, norm orientation, full residual Jacobian, uniqueness, and general O3a remain open.
nodes.method_family: Moving-event Wronskians, Pohozaev identities, Chebyshev event counting, uniform transfer bounds, blown-up paired-event implicit-function analysis, and one-point compactification of q
nodes.deliverable_contract: An exact all-root A_mu reduction and rigorous positivity on the fixed-n small-positive-contrast and fixed-finite-R large-q boundary regimes, without extending the result to the unresolved finite interior.
falsification_tests: Check the right-minus-left jump convention and the minus sign in rho_mu=-sum Delta_i t_(i,mu)delta_(t_i).
At R=1 prove exactly 2n simple labelled events for every finite q>=1; do not assume the word persists at q=1 without a double-root audit.
In the q-to-infinity limit prove paired event-velocity cancellation O(1/q), not merely boundedness of individual event velocities.
Keep the collapse estimates uniform only on bounded finite-contrast ranges and do not compactify a simultaneous R,q-to-infinity limit.
Do not use numerical scans, the implication-level wrong-sign scalar ledger, or the blocked phase-field subtraction as theorem premises.
nodes.expected_bottleneck: The exact event response J_mu is unsigned on the remaining finite-contrast bounded-q interior; accepted fixed-mu q-twist information controls J_q instead and does not orient J_mu.

nodes.title: Dual event Schur parity calibrates the minimum continuant orientation
nodes.statement: The accepted physical minimum relative-continuant representation and alternating event allocation, followed by two exact Sylvester determinant identities, imply the determinant-parity equivalence stated in CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-MIN-DETERMINANT-PARITY-R35.

nodes.title: Minimum dual-event determinant parity
nodes.statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, and arbitrary possibly asymmetric premise-complete event-transverse common-terminal minimum-law root with 2n events, let L_- be the accepted (2n-1)-dimensional relative path matrix. Split the n positive odd edges and n-1 negative even edges in the dual event matrix M=P-C^T W^(-1)C, with P>0 and W>0, and put H=C P^(-1)C^T-W. Then sign det(L_-)=sign det(H), including the zero-determinant case. Hence the exact R7 minimum orientation requirement is det(H)>0. For n=2 this agrees with H>0; for n>=3 it is algebraically strictly weaker than positive definiteness. The claim does not prove det(H)>0, root order, reflection symmetry, uniqueness, or existence.

nodes.title: Properness transports the mu=2 minimum anchor to a compact spectral strip
nodes.statement: Finite-contrast properness and relay-coordinate continuity, combined with local implicit uniqueness at reflection-fixed anchor roots, prove a compact anchor-slice lemma. Applying the trusted n=2 mu=2 twist and global order and the trusted n>=3 mu=2 nonexistence theorem gives the two strip conclusions in CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-MIN-COMPACT-MU2-STRIP-R35.

nodes.title: Compact finite-contrast minimum reflection and exclusion strips near mu=2
nodes.statement: Fix a compact finite-contrast interval K=[1+eta,M] with eta>0 and M<infinity. There is delta_2(K)>0 such that every premise-complete min-self-consistent four-switch point with R in K and |mu-2|<delta_2(K) is reflection invariant. For every fixed integer n>=3 there is delta_n(K)>0 such that no premise-complete min-self-consistent 2n-switch point with R in K has |mu-2|<delta_n(K). More generally, for any fixed n, fixed relay sign, and anchor mu_0>1 on such a compact K, reflection fixing plus nonzero partial_q A_n at every anchor root yields a uniform reflection-only neighborhood, while an empty anchor slice yields a uniform empty neighborhood. The widths need not be effective or uniform in n, and no statement is made for arbitrary mu, R down to 1, or unbounded R.

nodes.title: Orient the minimum dual-event determinant
nodes.statement: Prove det(H)>0 for every physical premise-complete event-transverse minimum-law common-terminal root, or produce an exact or rigorously certified violating root.
nodes.formal_statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, mu>1, and arbitrary possibly asymmetric premise-complete event-transverse minimum-law common-terminal root, form the physical dual negative-edge Schur matrix H=C P^(-1)C^T-W from CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-MIN-DETERMINANT-PARITY-R35. Prove det(H)>0; equivalently prove det(L_-)>0, J<0, and partial_q A_n<0. Alternatively certify a fully physical root with det(H)<=0.
discharge_criteria: Cover every finite R>1, n>=2, and mu>1, every relay chamber and compatible closure, and arbitrary asymmetric common-terminal roots.
Prove determinant positivity itself; do not replace it by the unnecessarily stronger H>0 or complementary-inertia assertion for n>=3.
Retain the relative scaling quotient and every event saltation coefficient, endpoint cell, parity, terminal soft-pair limit, and possible q-Jacobi singular root.

A counterexample must satisfy the complete physical relay, common-terminal, event-count, sign-law, phase, transversality, and energy predicates; relaxed matrices, local interfaces, and finite floating searches do not discharge the obligation.

If determinant orientation is proved, invoke the accepted global chamber/closure bridge separately; do not infer full equal-norm uniqueness or the stronger canonical minimum claim from the local lemma alone.

nodes.title: Minimum-side global reflection program after determinant calibration
nodes.statement: The run proves compact mu=2 reflection or exclusion strips and calibrates the general-n local event target from H>0 to the strictly weaker det(H)>0. It also derives an exact ordered-involution/endpoint-norming reduction, extends finite n=2 interface coverage on bounded parameter faces, and performs a frozen numerical search that finds no asymmetric or singular candidate. Arbitrary-mu all-n reflection remains open at either the physical determinant sign or a direct cross-root endpoint-order bridge; incomplete finite certificates and null searches are non-propagating.
nodes.method_family: Reflection involutions, terminal norming order, proper compact anchor continuation, event-matrix determinant parity, normalized boundary asymptotics, directed interval arithmetic, and deterministic falsification
nodes.deliverable_contract: A proof or refutation of reflection fixing for every finite-contrast minimum-law self-consistent exact-2n-switch point, with exact weaker lemmas integrated and every uncovered frequency, contrast, event boundary, and disconnected component explicit.
falsification_tests: Keep arbitrary asymmetric roots until reflection fixing is proved; do not work only in the symmetric ansatz.
Audit n=2 at arbitrary mu, n>=3, mu down to 1, large mu, both endpoint norming factors, and reflection two-cycles.
Do not infer all-root symmetry from properness, degree, or a surviving symmetric branch; an exact pitchfork model refutes that mechanism.
Do not promote finite binary64 or high-precision null searches, single-face interval certificates, or relaxed algebraic witnesses to a universal theorem or counterexample.
Distinguish determinant orientation from positive definiteness for n>=3 and retain the permanent scaling quotient correctly.
nodes.expected_bottleneck: The general-n physical dual determinant is unsigned. A mechanism-distinct direct route also lacks any accepted identity comparing endpoint norming data across two distinct equal-integral minimum roots; one-root action identities leave the alternating endpoint defect uncontrolled.

nodes.title: Path-forest expansion of the minimum dual determinant
nodes.statement: The accepted minimum dual-event matrix, its positive odd-cell blocks, and the alternating transverse event word imply the signed rooted-forest and positive-jump scaled determinant identities stated in CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-MIN-FOREST-CHARGE-R36.

nodes.title: Signed forest and interval-charge formula for the minimum determinant
nodes.statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, and arbitrary possibly asymmetric premise-complete event-transverse common-terminal minimum-law root, put N=n-1 and let H=C P^(-1)C^T-W be the accepted dual negative-edge Schur matrix. There are strictly positive path conductances tau_i and real vertex charges z_i such that H=L_tau+diag(z). If E ranges over retained edge subsets and Comp(E) over their interval components, then det(H)=sum_E (product_(i in E) tau_i) (product_(I in Comp(E)) sum_(j in I)z_j), including det(H)=0. Moreover, for the strictly positive physical event-jump vector v_i=(gamma_(2i+1)-gamma_(2i))/W_i, put q_i=v_i(Hv)_i and e_i=s_(i+1)v_i v_(i+1)>0. Then (product_i v_i^2)det(H) is the same forest polynomial with tau_i replaced by e_i and every interval charge replaced by Q_I=sum_(i in I)q_i. No sign of the interval charges, det(H)>0, reflection symmetry, uniqueness, or existence follows from these identities alone.

nodes.title: Positive-cell defect decomposition and common translation drift
nodes.statement: Exact two-frequency propagation on each positive minimum cell, direct low-mode energy jumps at all relay events, and monodromy conjugation under common spatial translation imply the defect and drift identities stated in CLM-NGE2-MPO3A-MIN-DEFECT-TRANSLATION-R36.

nodes.title: Minimum endpoint defect as positive-cell drift and common translation speed
nodes.statement: For every finite R>1, integer n>=2, mu>1, and arbitrary possibly asymmetric premise-complete event-transverse equal-norm minimum full-relay root, normalize the low mode by U_t(0)=1, put p=U_t(L), D=p^2-1, and C0=q^2-1>0. For each of the n internal positive cells let 0<theta_a<pi/(mu+1), z_a>0 be its positive low-mode amplitude ratio, k_mu(theta)=sin((mu-1)theta/2)/sin((mu+1)theta/2), and E_mu(theta,z)=(sin(mu theta)^2-sin(theta)^2)(1/k_mu-z)(z-k_mu)/(sin(theta)^2 sin(mu theta)^2). Then k_mu<z_a<1/k_mu and D=(R-1)C0 sum_a Phi_mu(theta_a,z_a), where Phi_mu=(z^2-1)/E_mu and Phi_mu(theta,1/z)=-Phi_mu(theta,z). Strict first-crossing physical positive cells occur with either sign of Phi, so no cellwise fixed-sign conclusion is valid. If all interfaces are translated through the common endpoint material, the adjacent Dirichlet eigenvalues have the same first derivative D/I at a complete equal-norm root. Thus first-order translation cancels from their gap and supplies neither a one-sided sign of D nor global reflection symmetry.
